title: Morton's estate, the Library of Congress material and his relatives
summary: Court order for library items, who inherits, his sister in Los Angeles, and Dink Johnson as brother-in-law.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Talking about my children and grandchildren

blocks.x: Well, getting back to the library, just to bring this thing a little bit into some sort of perspective, I remember that Lesh went in there and got a court order for those, didn't he?
He got a court order from the estate, yes. The estate gave him an order. He gave him an order to take out everything.
The estate, who would that have been? His wife?

No, it was his sister. His sister and the woman that he had been familiar with before. She might have been his wife one day, but she was married to another guy at that time, so she wasn't his wife then. Anyhow, that was two things provided for in his will and that's what the estate stands for. Except that what I pay goes to his sister. She's still living? She's still living, yes.
She's still on the west coast?
Yeah, Los Angeles. She was in New Orleans at first, you know. She had a couple of children, I think, in Los Angeles. Or they went shortly after. I saw her one time in New Orleans.
Was that lawyer Hugh Macbeth still around?
He died and his nephew is the administrator.
Well, who is, what was the relationship between Jelly and Dink Johnson? There was some in-law.

Brother-in-law. Brother-in-law, I think. I think Dink was the brother of his first wife, whoever she was. That's as near as I can guess. This woman claimed she was still the one, but she was married to a guy by the name of Ford right at that time, you know, out there. Well, they all were bald. I tried to get a lawyer in New York.
